title: Implement SoA (Structure of Arrays) batch layout for GF(p^n) SIMD
description:
Implement Structure of Arrays (SoA) batch layout for GF(p^n) extension field elements, enabling vertical SIMD processing where each SIMD lane handles the same coefficient position across multiple independent field elements, AND deliver the AVX2 `Fp<65537>` base-field batch kernel required to hit the ≥3× speedup criterion. ## Motivation Standard Array of Structures (AoS) layout for GF(p^n) elements: ``` [{c0, c1, c2, c3}, {c0, c1, c2, c3}, {c0, c1, c2, c3}, ...] ``` Polynomial multiplication has cross-lane dependencies between coefficients, which makes AoS awkward for SIMD. The SoA layout transposes the data: ``` c0: [elem0.c0, elem1.c0, elem2.c0, elem3.c0, ...] ← one SIMD vector c1: [elem0.c1, elem1.c1, elem2.c1, elem3.c1, ...] ← one SIMD vector c2: [elem0.c2, elem1.c2, elem2.c2, elem3.c2, ...] ← one SIMD vector c3: [elem0.c3, elem1.c3, elem2.c3, elem3.c3, ...] ← one SIMD vector ``` The polynomial logic operates at the high level (combining coefficient vectors according to the extension field multiplication formula), while the coefficient arithmetic (GF(p) multiply, add) is vectorised across SIMD lanes — processing 4 or 8 independent elements simultaneously. ## Core type (delivered in session 2, retained) ```rust /// Batch of GF(p^n) elements stored in Structure of Arrays layout /// for SIMD-friendly access. pub struct BatchExtField { coeffs: [Vec; N], } impl BatchExtField { fn len(&self) -> usize; fn from_elements(elements: &[impl ExtensionField]) -> Self; fn to_elements(&self) -> Vec>; fn batch_mul(&self, other: &Self) -> Self; fn batch_add(&self, other: &Self) -> Self; } ``` ## SIMD execution model For `BatchExtField, 2>` (batch of GF(p²) quadratic extension elements), Karatsuba multiplication is three base-field batch multiplies over contiguous `&[Fp

]` slices plus a handful of base-field vector adds/subs. ## Expanded scope: AVX2 Fp<65537> batch kernel (2026-04-19) Session 2 delivered the SoA layout and the `batch_mul_quadratic` straight-line kernel, but the benchmark recorded 0.92× (i.e. slower than the AoS scalar baseline) at `N = 1000` GF(p²) elements over `Fp<65537>`. The auto-vectoriser does not generate packed `Fp<65537>` multiplications on Zen 3. The SoA layout is only useful when coupled with an explicit base-field SIMD kernel. Under the "everyone's responsibility — no deferred quality issues" policy, the 3× benchmark criterion is met in this same issue, not deferred to a follow-up. ### Required Add an AVX2 batch kernel for `Fp<65537>` in `gf2-kernels-simd` and wire it through `FieldVec>::mul_vec` so that `BatchExtField::batch_mul_quadratic` picks it up. **Kernel shape:** - New file `crates/gf2-kernels-simd/src/fp65537.rs` (or extend `mersenne.rs` if reuse is cleaner) targeting `Fp<65537>`. - Input canonical values `< 65537` in packed `u32` lanes (8 lanes per 256-bit AVX2 vector). - Multiplication: 32-bit products fit in `u64` per lane; reduce `x mod (2^16 + 1)` using the identity `x = x_hi * 2^16 + x_lo`, and `2^16 ≡ -1 (mod 65537)`, so `x mod p = (x_lo − x_hi) mod p`. Two branchless canonicalisation steps then bring results into `[0, p)`. - Output canonical `u32` lanes. - Safe function-pointer wrapper exposed through a detector analogous to `MersenneFns`, returning `Option`. - Runtime dispatch via the existing `OnceLock` in `gf2-core/src/lib.rs`. **Wiring:** - Extend `FieldVec>::mul_vec`, `add_vec`, `sub_vec` to route through the new kernel when the runtime dispatch table returns `Some(Fp65537Fns)`. - `BatchExtField::batch_mul_quadratic` already consumes contiguous `&[F]` slices; no API change needed. Confirm end-to-end. ### Regression and performance proof - Unit tests comparing the SIMD kernel output to scalar `Fp<65537>::mul` for random and edge-case inputs (0, 1, p-1, saturated lanes). - Proptest with ≤64 cases: for random `a`, `b` batches of length 1…1024, `simd_mul(a, b) == scalar_mul(a, b)` elementwise. - Re-run `cargo bench -p gf2-core --bench soa_batch -- --quick` and record the new `BatchExtField::batch_mul_quadratic` time. Paste the table into the module docstring of `gfpn/batch.rs`, replacing the current 0.92× row. - Criterion confidence interval must show the SoA batch path is ≥3× faster than sequential scalar `QuadraticExt::mul` at `N = 1000`. ## Conversion cost (carry-over note) AoS↔SoA conversion involves a transpose. For small batches this overhead can dominate; SoA is beneficial when processing large vectors/matrices of extension field elements, when the data originates in SoA layout, or when multiple operations happen before converting back. ## Location - `crates/gf2-core/src/gfpn/batch.rs` (SoA layout — already exists) - `crates/gf2-kernels-simd/src/fp65537.rs` or extensions to `mersenne.rs` (new kernel) - `crates/gf2-core/src/field/fieldvec.rs` (wiring — already exists; add Fp<65537> dispatch) ## Dependencies - `3f4b946c` (tower extension field architecture) — done. - `0fb99491` (SIMD-accelerated FieldVec operations with delayed reduction) — done. ## Success criteria - `BatchExtField::batch_mul` produces identical results to element-wise scalar multiplication (existing criterion). - AoS→SoA→AoS round-trip preserves all elements exactly (existing criterion). - **Benchmark: SoA batch multiplication of 1000 GF(p²) elements over `Fp<65537>` is ≥3× faster than sequential scalar multiplication. The measured speedup is recorded in the module docstring.** - **AVX2 `Fp<65537>` batch multiply kernel in `gf2-kernels-simd` with runtime dispatch via `OnceLock`.** - Unit tests + proptests comparing the new SIMD kernel to scalar `Fp<65537>` arithmetic for random and edge-case inputs. - All three gates pass: `code-review`, `doc-review`, `cargo-ci`. - Unsafe code isolated to `gf2-kernels-simd` (`#![deny(unsafe_code)]` preserved in `gf2-core`). - Non-AVX2 hosts (and AVX2-disabled builds) fall back cleanly to scalar arithmetic. ## Host target AMD Ryzen 9 5900X (Zen 3): AVX2, PCLMUL, VAES, SHA-NI. **No AVX-512.** The kernel must not require AVX-512. ## Breakdown reference - `dev/active/e095a100-handoff-2.md` — scope expansion authorised 2026-04-19. - Session 2 benchmark: 0.92× (commit a6cca7b + d3938cb).
